restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224). Total work over all processors: T = 30,789,931,306,303 first-block C_32 trials at 1 unit plus 64 operations each, a hard counter cap of 254 T operations on all Step-2/3 work, 8 units of output verification, table build C = 2^38, starting solution D = 2^38 and characteristic search E = 32 * 593,858 CPU-s * 3,354,001 units per CPU-s = 2^45.8572 units; total 99,479,814,703,862 units = 2^46.49947.

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes with M1 != M1'; complete SHA-256 with the standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 output bits; every output is recomputed before it is returned.

32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang and Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080): its Fig. 6 characteristic, its 71 two-bit conditions under the stated readings and its starting solution as advice. The table and Step-2/3 specification follow hash-smash #26/#33 (winglock), restated in proof Sections 4-5.

One run with no restarts. Success probability >= 0.390109 from fresh independent first blocks, conditional on the declared rate heuristics, after subtracting a Chebyshev bound of 9.220e-4 on stopping at the counter cap, with the mean-work bound corrected to E[X] <= 238.943. No certificate is supplied.

Measured inputs are credited public participant measurements (#296, #396, #26, #227), not runs made for this package: the matching rate q, the Step-2/3 stage pass rates, the table moments, the completed characteristic-search ledger and the callgrind CPU-second calibration. Our own checks (proof Section 14) are exact finite checks only. Our own measurements (proof Section 15) are a per-instruction costing of the x86-64 CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21 code, a callgrind dynamic per-form profile of that exact library on four SHA-256 CNF solves, and 17 CryptoMiniSat instruction-rate runs on SHA-256 CNF. They support the CPU-second price and do not re-run the charged search. This derivative inherits the credited model unchanged; it retunes T to 30,789,931,306,303 at w = 254 under the corrected cap-stop denominator of leech1996's public 83bc57d and claims the integer-tight 46.4995. The full characteristic search E, table C, and starting solution D remain charged.

heuristics.statement: A first block M0 of fresh uniform words, compressed as CV1 = C_32(IV, M0), yields at least q = 2^-17.3583 expected valid tuples (records passing Step 2 tests (a)-(g)) against TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 records, and at most 2^-17.3166.
heuristics.scope: The exact P1-P4 sets and the Step-2 tests of proof Sections 4-5, with C_32 first blocks from the standard IV.
heuristics.extrapolation: Public participant measurement #296: four runs of 2^32 C_32 first blocks, one per index-part of TAB2, 25,936 valid tuples, pooled 2^-17.3373 with 99% interval [2^-17.3583, 2^-17.3166]. Corroborated by #26's runs (2^-17.3337), the #227 campaign counts (2^-17.326) and the analytic prediction 2^-17.3254. Extrapolated to T = 30,789,931,306,303 fresh trials.
heuristics.limitations: Credited participant runs, not organizer executions and not repeated for this package. CV1 words are treated as uniform for the Step-2 tests.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple, each of the 196,608 P4 entries passes Step-3 stages 16..31 with probability at least p = 2^-46, and at least one entry passes with probability r >= 2^-28.415 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Second-block steps 16..22 and schedule words W16..W31 under the Fig. 6 characteristic. Entries share W14 in 12 groups of 2^14; the shared W20 conditions are charged in the second moment.
heuristics.extrapolation: The condition count is 45 printed by S plus the unprinted E16[29] = E17[29] (#26). #296's cumulative stage rates over 2^32.248 candidates match the count through step 21 (2^-3.000, 2^-15.000, then 22, 5 and 1 survivors). The 13 W20/W22 carry conditions after step 21 are extrapolated. Both S's published tuple and the public 32-step pair of #227 pass every stage in our checks.
heuristics.limitations: Independence beyond the W14 grouping is assumed, not proved. One extra independent condition would lower the success bound to 0.2949 at this T (proof Section 13).

heuristics.statement: For the number V of valid tuples in one trial, E[C(V,2)] <= q * 2^-5.
heuristics.scope: Valid tuples produced from one first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: #296 observed 9 within-part pairs in 2^34 part-trials and bounded the cross-part pairs from multiplicity sums. The charged 2^-5 exceeds that estimate by more than 20x.
heuristics.limitations: Cross-part pairs were not observed directly. This is a credited participant measurement.

heuristics.statement: Constructing the Fig. 6 characteristic by S's four-step SAT/SMT search, without S's intermediate outputs, costs at most 32 * 593,858 solver CPU-seconds on the measurement machine.
heuristics.scope: The one-time characteristic search, charged in preprocessing as E. Its memory is covered by search-peak-memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: #396 ran S's procedure with the authors' public model and STP 2.3.4 + CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21. Its 59 calls, all charged including timeouts and abandoned calls, used 593,858 CPU-s, and the run returned a characteristic whose signed rows equal Fig. 6. Because the run used S's nabla W and S's tA threshold, #396 priced a blind re-derivation from its own call ledger at 6.3-8.4 times that, and added a residual factor 4 for solver variance and model choice. The product 32 is adopted unchanged.
heuristics.limitations: S's own search time is unpublished. The factor 32 is argued from a measured ledger, not executed. tE4 = 76 was reached but not proved optimal. Doubling the factor raises the total to 2^47.253.

heuristics.statement: One solver CPU-second on the measurement machine costs at most kappa = 3,354,001 target-compression units (2^21.677 units, 2^32.796 primitive word operations). This is 6.82 operations per retired instruction at the calibrated 2^30.026 instructions per CPU-second.
heuristics.scope: The STP + CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21 calls priced in E and D, on the machine that ran them. No price is claimed for any other machine.
heuristics.extrapolation: kappa = ceil(R_cal * m_dyn * S / C). R_cal: callgrind calibration (#296/#396), 44,197,378,388 instructions in 40.42 native CPU-s (repeats 41.07 and 41.10), i.e. 2^30.026 per CPU-s, from one single-threaded call. m_dyn = 3.6874: our callgrind profile of the exact x86-64 CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21 library (SHA-256 878e2f2b...8659c0) on four SHA-256 CNF solves (19.1-23.1e9 executed instructions each, solve call only, all objects, 0 unmatched addresses), every executed instruction priced by its form under the v5 primitive list, gives ordinary means 1.880-1.956; we take 1.956 and combine it with the calibrated call's class shares (7.24% PLT stubs at 3, 0.416% divide/multiply/floating point at 400, above our measured 0.21-0.30%). Every profiled run's own all-inclusive mean (2.797-3.106) is at least 19% below m_dyn. S = 1.85: our 14 single-thread CryptoMiniSat runs on SHA-256 CNF (9 instance shapes, 1-3 seeds, up to 281 CPU-s) varied in instructions per CPU-s by at most 1.842 (max/min) on one machine. Long runs, larger resident sets and 4 threads lowered the rate or left it unchanged (0.84-1.00x).
heuristics.limitations: The instruction rate of the 59 charged calls was not measured; it is assumed to be within 1.85x of the one calibrated call. Our rate runs used another machine, instruction set and solver build (Apple M4 Pro, arm64, CryptoMiniSat 5.16.0); they enter only as a relative spread. The dynamic profile used the exact x86-64 library but through its Python binding on our SHA-256 CNF, single threaded, not inside STP on the charged model; the STP front end is not profiled and the STP-linked build may use other compiler flags. No organizer experiment can re-measure the rate. An ordinary mean of 3 operations gives 46.778; the class price of our previous package gives 47.140.

heuristics.statement: Producing the Step-1 starting solution (the advice words A4..A13, E8..E13, W12, W13) costs at most 2^38 units.
heuristics.scope: One SAT solution of the characteristic through step 13, charged once as D.
heuristics.extrapolation: S reports about 2^34.3, with no unit; read as 35-step compressions this is below 2^34.46 units. #296's two exact-value-model runs of the same task took 908.8 CPU-s in total, which gives 2^37.36 units at the kappa of cpu-second-pricing with a factor 32 (2^37.83 at kappa = 2^23). D = 2^38 covers both readings.
heuristics.limitations: S's unit and trace are unpublished. D is below 0.3% of the total, so this does not change the claimed exponent at two decimals.

heuristics.statement: The per-trial counted Step-2/3 operations X satisfy E[X] <= 238.943 and E[X^2] <= 6.436e12 under the charges of proof Section 5.4. The displayed component sum 238.94281 truncates downward; the upper bound 238.943 is used.
heuristics.scope: Only the probability of stopping at the counter cap of 254 T. The time bound itself is a hard cap and does not depend on this.
heuristics.extrapolation: Inputs are the exact occupancy mean N/2^27, the measured maximum bucket of 936, the multiplicity sum 5.758e9 (Cauchy-Schwarz over 4 parts), the Step-2 cumulative pass fractions bounded by 0.51, 1/15, 1/120 and 1/240, the Step-3 stage-16/17 pass fractions bounded by 2^-2.99 and 2^-14.9, and q at its upper limit. The quantities come from #296. Chebyshev with the denominator (254 - 238.943)^2 = 226.713249 gives a cap-stop probability <= 9.220e-4.
heuristics.limitations: Credited measurements. A 100x larger second moment pushes the cap-stop to 0.0922 and the success bound to 0.2988, below 0.39 (proof Section 13).

heuristics.statement: The characteristic and starting-solution searches need at most 2^33 bytes of memory at their peak.
heuristics.scope: Memory only. The searches run before the attack phase.
heuristics.extrapolation: #296 and #396 measured a peak resident set of 5.25 GiB over all calls. It is added to the attack memory anyway: 28,661,817,348 bytes = 2^34.739.
heuristics.limitations: S's own search memory is not reported. Memory does not affect the score.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple drawn uniformly from the multiset of valid tuples of a trial conditioned on V >= 1, the probability that some P4 entry passes Step 3 is at least the per-tuple marginal r >= 2^-28.415 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Trials of the Section 4 algorithm against the fixed P4 and TAB2 of Section 8.
heuristics.extrapolation: Step-3 conditions read only the tuple's W14/W20 words and fixed P4 entries, disjoint from the Step-2 tests (a)-(g) certifying validity, so the pass probability of a tuple selected conditional on V >= 1 equals the pooled marginal measured by step3-46-conditions. The #227 instance passed Step 3 on an independently found valid tuple at the predicted rate.
heuristics.limitations: Declared independence assumption: no proof that conditioning on V >= 1 does not bias tuple shapes toward Step-3 failures. If the true conditional rate were a factor 2 below r, the success bound falls to 0.2187 at this T, below the claimed 0.39 (proof Section 13).
